::: {.callout-warning}
## Exposure risk
Exposing Crisalid AI on the web without proper security puts you at risk of:

- **Data leaks** — institutional or personal data from the knowledge graph accessible to unauthorised users
- **LLM exhaustion** — uncontrolled consumption of tokens, which is critical with pay-per-token or quota-limited providers
:::

Crisalid AI's [four-layer architecture](index.qmd#architecture) means that security must be configured at each layer independently. The sections below cover each layer from the graph up.

---

## 🕸️ The graph layer — Neo4j

Neo4j is secured by a **username and password**, configured in `docker/neo4j/.env`.

::: {.callout-important}
## No RBAC in Neo4j Community Edition
Neo4j Community Edition does not support role-based access control (RBAC). All authenticated users have the same level of access to the graph. For fine-grained access control, the Enterprise Edition is required.

In a Community Edition deployment, the choice of toolset (`crisalid-restricted` vs `crisalid-unrestricted`) is the primary access control mechanism — see [the tools layer](#the-tools-layer-neo4j-mcp) below.
:::

In production, avoid storing the Neo4j password in plain-text `.env` files. Use a sovereign secret management solution such as [HashiCorp Vault](https://www.vaultproject.io/).

---

## 🛠️ The tools layer — Neo4j MCP

The [Neo4j MCP Toolbox](https://neo4j.com/labs/genai-ecosystem/mcp-toolbox/) does **not** support passwords or API keys. Authentication relies exclusively on **JWT tokens** issued by an OIDC provider — in the Crisalid stack, this is **Keycloak**.

Each client application (such as `crisalid-agents-owui` or `crisalid-agents-chat-api`) must be provisioned with a **Keycloak service account** to obtain tokens. This setup requires the Keycloak component of the Crisalid stack to be deployed and running.

::: {.callout-note}
## Local workstation
The Keycloak requirement makes MCP toolbox authentication impractical on a local workstation. For local development, leave `KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID` and `KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET` empty in `docker/crisalid-agents/.env` — the toolbox client will then connect without authentication (suitable for a trusted local environment only).
:::

Port 5000 is **not exposed on the host** — it is only reachable inside the Docker network. See the [local workstation](local-workstation.qmd) page if you need to access it from outside the stack.

For the full Keycloak service account setup procedure, see [Using CRISalid AI Skills](using-skills.qmd).

---

## 🤖 The agent layer — Crisalid Agents (OpenWebUI Pipelines)

[OpenWebUI Pipelines](https://github.com/open-webui/pipelines) exposes a FastAPI server on port 9099. This endpoint is secured by a **shared API key** (`PIPELINES_API_KEY`).

The key is set once and must be provided by any client connecting to the pipelines server — in the Crisalid stack, this client is OpenWebUI itself.

**In the Docker deployment**, the key is configured in the shared `docker/.env`:

```bash
CRISALID_AGENTS_PIPELINES_API_KEY=<your-secret-key>
```

It is injected into `crisalid-agents-owui` as `PIPELINES_API_KEY` — the server uses it to authenticate incoming requests.

When adding the pipelines connection in OpenWebUI (**Admin panel → Settings → Connections**, URL `http://crisalid-agents-owui:9099`), enter this key by hand in the API key field.

Port 9099 is **not exposed on the host** — it is only reachable inside the Docker network (`agents-network`).

### The chat API (`crisalid-agents-chat-api`)

A second agent service exposes the same graph agent as a streaming chat API for SoVisuPlus (port 9100). It is secured by **API keys**: the `x-api-key` request header is checked against the comma-separated `CHAT_API_KEYS` list in `docker/crisalid-agents/.env`. SoVisuPlus authenticates with the key set as `SVP_CRISALID_CHAT_API_KEY` in `docker/sovisuplus/.env`, which must be one of the `CHAT_API_KEYS` values.

Port 9100 is **not exposed on the host** — the chat API is only reachable inside the Docker network (`crisalid-front`), server-to-server.

---

## 🖥️ The interface layer — OpenWebUI

OpenWebUI is the only layer directly exposed to end users.

- **User registration is disabled** by default (`ENABLE_SIGNUP=false`) — accounts must be created manually by an administrator, or provisioned through Keycloak SSO.
- An **admin account is seeded** on first run via `OPENWEBUI_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `OPENWEBUI_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in `docker/openwebui/.env`.
- **Keycloak SSO** can be enabled via OAuth2/OIDC — see [Configuring OpenWebUI](configuring-openwebui.qmd).
